evidence.note: resultBlockers validates schema version, id, kind, verdict, reviewer, RFC3339 reviewedAt, shard-id pattern, file-name agreement, evidence and per-finding severity/disposition; the medium+ non-closing disposition rule at line 503 matches the documented blocking contract.

Injection handling is correct: markdown.PlainText runs BEFORE the mrvf- neutralisation, so a control character cannot be used to reassemble a finding-ID token after stripping; escapePipes runs after markdown.InlineCode, and GFM row splitting on pipes is handled as documented. findingIDPattern in internal/reviewlog/reviewlog.go:53 is lowercase-only, so the case-sensitive replacement is sufficient.

The source change is covered by 31 tests in the same package, including table-cell forgery, evidence-rule parity with the validator, duplicate shard results, cross-shard plan-hash freshness, and oversize/malformed result handling. `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean for internal/reviewmanifest, internal/fsm/machine and internal/fsm/run.

shardIDPattern (manifest.go:60) accepts shard-[0-9a-f]{1,3}(-N)? and shardIDForPath emits ceil(bits/4) hex digits with maxBucketBits=12 (shards.go:18), so the pattern cannot reject a legitimately generated shard id. Verified against the repo, not inferred from the diff.

The three hashes are the external sha256 oracle regenerated by testdata/oracle.sh (never Go) and are asserted line-by-line against LineHash and the prev-chain in internal/fsm/run/store_test.go:813-828, including a one-byte-edit negative case. Fixture is genuinely load-bearing, not dead data.

The part-2 test chunk adds torn-log/repair, sidecar, stamp, exit and append-failure-sweep coverage. The nested store-failure sweeps are O(n^2) in append sites, but `go test -count=1 ./internal/fsm/machine/` completes in 0.75s, so there is no runtime concern. No TODO/FIXME, no eval, no exec of untrusted input anywhere in the shard.

findings.note: sourceAssignmentBlockers claims in its own doc comment that 'every chunk lands in exactly one shard', but it only detects duplicate (path, part) keys and unassigned paths. It never checks that all chunk.Parts parts of a chunked file are present, so a plan that dropped part 2 of 3 would pass the assignment check with the path still marked seen. The Parts field is available (it is used by chunkedFileLines at manifest.go:774). Low because the plan is generated in-process by contextprofile rather than supplied by an agent.

Duplicate shard results raise a 'duplicate shard result' blocker (manifest.go:414), but there is no counterpart for cross-shard results: Input/Manifest carry a single *ReviewResult, so if more than one result file declares kind cross-shard with the current plan hash, the last one read silently replaces the earlier one with neither a blocker nor an IgnoredResult reason. Reachability is limited because a second such file would have to be named shard-*.result.json, which then trips the file-name blocker at manifest.go:487, so the failure mode is fail-closed rather than fail-open. Asymmetry worth closing for auditability of the committed log.

MaxResultBytes is described as an accident guard on a result file's size, but ParseResult can only apply it after the caller has already read the entire file into memory (shardpack.Discover reads with deps.ReadFile then calls ParseResult). The guard therefore bounds what is parsed, not what is read. Fine as an accident guard by its own stated intent; noted so the comment is not later read as a resource bound.
